title: Posting Insurance Proceeds to Water Damage Mitigation Jobs
content:
This guidance governs how carrier payments recorded on an Insurance Claim Services file are posted to a Water Damage Mitigation job.

## Rule
The job must be in authorized, drying, drying complete or invoiced status when insurance proceeds are posted. The carrier payment must be recorded on the same claim file this job is linked to. Only dwelling-coverage carrier payments that reached the company, by direct payment or by a two-party check the customer has endorsed, are posted to a water job; payments routed to a mortgagee loss-draft account reach the company only through rebuild draws and are never posted here, and contents-coverage payments belong to contents jobs. A carrier payment is posted to the same water job at most once. The amount posted is the lesser of the job's balance due at posting and the carrier payment's unapplied remainder, where the unapplied remainder is the carrier payment amount less every posting already made from that same carrier payment to any water, fire, mold or rebuild job; when one carrier payment must cover several jobs, the order in which they are paid follows the claim payment allocation rule of the Insurance Claim Services charter.

## What may be posted
| Carrier payment | Posted to a water job? |
|---|---|
| Dwelling coverage, paid directly to the company | yes |
| Dwelling coverage, two-party check the customer has endorsed | yes |
| Routed to a mortgagee loss-draft account | no; it reaches the company only through rebuild draws |
| Contents coverage | no; it belongs to contents jobs |
| Recorded on a different claim file from the job's | no |
| Already posted to this same water job | no; at most once per job |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)
A carrier payment of $6000.00 has already been posted for $4500.00 to a fire job. Its unapplied remainder is $1500.00. A water job on the same claim file with a balance due of $2200.00 receives the lesser of $2200.00 and $1500.00, that is $1500.00; with a balance due of $900.00 it would receive $900.00.
